title: [YouPass Collect] - The proportion of holidaymakers using four different types of accommodation
prompt: The charts below show the proportion of holidaymakers using four different types of accommodation in three different years. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the percentages of holidaymakers choosing four different types of accommodation over a period of 20 years, namely 1988, 1998 and 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, staying with family remained the most popular choice throughout the period shown, despite experiencing a decline towards the end. Additionally, while the proportion of people camping decreased significantly, there were notable rises in those opting for both hotels and rented apartments.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the two most common types of accommodation, enjoying holidays at their family's homes accounted for more than half of all holidaymakers in 1988, at 52%. This figure saw a slight increase to 54% in 1998, before dropping to 44% in the final year. Meanwhile, hotels were chosen by only 15% of travelers in 1988, but this proportion rose to 22% in both 1998 and 2008.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining options, camping was initially the second most popular choice, selected by approximately a quarter of holidaymakers in 1988. However, this figure halved to 13% in 1998 and continued to decline slightly to 12% in 2008. In contrast, rented apartments showed a steady upward trend, rising from just 7% in 1988 to 11% a decade later, before doubling to 22% by the end of the period.
